issueOrPullRequest.title: feat: make the canonical skills configuration-aware
issueOrPullRequest.body:
## Governing issue

Closes #33

## Summary

This change makes the canonical skills read project configuration from `.garage/config.yaml`.

- **Reading configuration.** A skill reads a value only at a step that cites an extension point, and only after `garage config validate` succeeds. It stops and escalates if the binary is missing, if validation fails, or if a required value has no default.
- **Integration branch.** The configured integration branch (E1) replaces the hardcoded `staging` PR target. `staging` remains only as the default.
- **Rules and roles.** Each skill states the responsibility-floor rules it enforces, and rejects instructions that conflict with its role or with the configuration. Vendor names are replaced with role-based wording.
- **Evidence format.** The Agent #1, Agent #2, and PR-equivalence record templates adopt `garage-evidence` and `garage-artifact-v1`. Agent #2 now stops if valid Agent #1 completion evidence is absent.
- **Frontmatter and recording.**
  - Each skill gains `metadata.garage-role`.
  - Each role makes one best-effort `garage record` attempt after its GitHub record is verified.
  - The existing `description` values are now quoted, so the frontmatter parses as strict YAML.
- **Docs.** The configuration, registry, floor, review-evidence, adoption, README, GOVERNANCE, and CONTRIBUTING docs now describe how the skills behave after this change.

## Independent engineering review

- Review record: [Agent #2 implementation review on #33](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/33#issuecomment-6852033450), APPROVED. It is the authoritative record of the review.
- Reviewer: Agent #2, in an execution context separate from the implementation. The separation is an assertion recorded in that review.

- [x] The reviewer did not implement this change.
- [x] Any required corrections were made and independently re-reviewed. No corrections were required.
- [x] This pull request contains the change that was approved, and nothing else. The head's `garage-artifact-v1` changeset equals the approved one; see the equivalence record on this PR.

## Validation

- `make check` (gofmt, vet, `go test ./...`, build, six-platform cross-compile): pass.
- `garage config validate` on Builder Garage's configuration: valid.
- The stop cases the skills rely on, checked against the real binary:

  | Case | Exit code |
  | --- | --- |
  | Absent configuration | 1 |
  | Invalid YAML | 1 |
  | Missing E5 and E8 values | 1 |
  | No `garage` binary | 127 |

- The frontmatter of all five skills parses as strict YAML, with the expected `garage-role` values.
- The shared configuration section and the shared artifact section are byte-identical across the skills that carry them. The embedded procedure equals the reference procedure in `docs/review-evidence.md`.
- Relative link and anchor check over all tracked Markdown: 0 broken. `git diff --check`: clean.

## Environment / Deployment Requirements

- After merge, refresh the installed skill copies at each configured target: the Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot CLI user paths.
- Agents need a `garage` binary on `PATH`, built from this repository, to resolve any configured value. There is no installation package yet. Without the binary, the updated skills stop at the first extension point they reach.

## Maintainer approval

Independent review approval does not authorize merge. A maintainer approves this pull request separately, and all required checks must pass.

## Maintainer decision: #35 before #33, and #33's adopted scope (2026-11-12)

This identical comment is posted on #33 and #35. It does not edit either issue body, change repository files, or create or close issues. Where an issue body conflicts with this decision, including #35's "Depends on: Configuration-aware canonical skills", this decision governs.

### Decisions

1. **Dependency order.** #35 comes before #33.
   - #35 defines and safely initializes the sole canonical project-configuration source, `.garage/config.yaml`.
   - #33 then teaches the canonical skills to read only valid configuration from that source.
   - The skills have no interim adoption-record lookup convention.

2. **The #34 evidence format in #33.** When #33 proceeds, it adopts `garage-evidence` and `garage-artifact-v1` ([docs/review-evidence.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/main/docs/review-evidence.md)) in the Agent #1, Agent #2, and PR-equivalence record templates.
   - Agent #2's prerequisite stop rule is defined against that structured evidence.
   - Records use a resolved base or ref rather than a bare `main`.
   - A triggered PR review uses `responds_to` to identify its equivalence record.

3. **Skill frontmatter.** #33 adds the stable source metadata key `metadata.garage-role`. #38 generates `metadata.garage-revision` when it embeds or installs the skill artifact, and binds it through its manifest and digest. No source placeholder is used.

4. **Private recording.** #33 adds one best-effort `garage record` attempt, made after the role has written and verified its durable GitHub Issue or PR record. A missing binary or a recording failure is ignored. Recording never gates, authorizes, advances, or coordinates workflow.

5. **Interim documentation.** [docs/extension-points.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/main/docs/extension-points.md) and [docs/responsibility-floor.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/main/docs/responsibility-floor.md) correctly describe the current interim adoption record until #35 lands. They do not establish a configuration-discovery path that #33 will implement.

### Readiness

Under this corrected dependency order, #35 requires its own readiness pass before implementation. #33 must not receive a readiness verdict until #35 is complete.

# Implementation Readiness: #33

Assessed under [implementation-readiness-workflow](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/skills/implementation-readiness-workflow/SKILL.md) against `main` at `fa30a65`, after #35 merged (PR #45). That satisfies the [#33/#35 decision](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/35#issuecomment-6839187808), which allows a #33 verdict only once #35 is complete. This was read-only. No files, settings, or other issues were changed.

## Decision

**NOT READY.** One prerequisite blocks implementation: the four maintainer answers below were given in a session and are not yet recorded on this issue. Under this project's practice, a decision that an implementation relies on needs its own durable maintainer record, which the implementation then cites. This report is not that record. When the maintainer records them, #33 is **READY**, with no other material unknowns.

## Acceptance Boundary

From the #33 body and the [#33/#35 decision](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/35#issuecomment-6839187808), which governs where the two conflict:

- The skills read project values only from `.garage/config.yaml`, and only at the extension points E1–E10 declared in [docs/extension-points.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/extension-points.md). There is no interim adoption-record lookup (decision item 1).
- Missing or invalid required configuration results in a stop and escalation, never a guessed value (AC2).
- The skills do not assign, invoke, wait for, poll, or otherwise orchestrate another agent (AC3).
- `staging` stops being a universal integration target. The PR target in [integration-pr-review](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/skills/integration-pr-review/SKILL.md) (step 5 under "No PR exists") becomes the configured E1 value, with `staging` as the default only when E1 is omitted (AC4). The other uses of "staging" in the skills name environments, not the integration branch, and are unaffected.
- An agent rejects instructions that conflict with its assigned role or the valid configuration.
- The language is role-based, so vendor and model establish no authority (F9).
- The Agent #1, Agent #2, and PR-equivalence record templates adopt `garage-evidence` and `garage-artifact-v1` from [docs/review-evidence.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/review-evidence.md). Agent #2's prerequisite stop is defined against that evidence. Records use a resolved base or ref, and a triggered PR review uses `responds_to` (decision item 2).
- Skill frontmatter gains `metadata.garage-role` (decision item 3).
- Each role makes one best-effort `garage record` attempt after it has written and verified its durable GitHub record. A missing binary or a recording failure is ignored (decision item 4).

**Maintainer answers given in session on 2026-11-13. Pending a durable record on this issue:**

1. **Determining validity.** A skill treats configuration as valid only when `garage config validate` succeeds. It then reads the needed value from `.garage/config.yaml`. If the binary is unavailable or validation fails, the skill stops and escalates. The agent does not judge validity itself.
2. **Where a skill stops.** A skill reads configuration only when it reaches an extension point that needs a project value. Absent or invalid configuration stops the skill at that point. Where a value is optional and omitted from a valid configuration, the canonical default applies. E5 and E8 have no default, so reaching them always requires a valid configuration.
3. **`metadata.garage-role` values.** These are functional names:
   - `implementer` for application-implementation-workflow and integration-pr-review, which both execute as Agent #1;
   - `reviewer` for independent-implementation-review;
   - `readiness` for implementation-readiness-workflow;
   - `discovery` for engineering-discovery-workflow.

   This follows the [#37](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/37) probe precedent and the `garage record` event types.
4. **E10 conditional guidance.** This is out of scope for #33. The Supabase guidance keeps applying under its own stated condition. The skills do not consume `guidance.conditional` names yet, and what a listed name means is left to a follow-up issue.

## Existing System / Patterns to Reuse

- [docs/configuration.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/configuration.md): the key shapes, defaults, and absent/invalid semantics.
- [docs/responsibility-floor.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/responsibility-floor.md#precedence): the precedence the skills must state, which is floor, then valid configuration, then canonical defaults.
- [docs/review-evidence.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/review-evidence.md): the evidence block, the record types, where each record lives, and the checked and asserted split. The templates are adopted from it, not redesigned.
- [`internal/cli/history.go`](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/internal/cli/history.go): its event types (`discovery`, `readiness`, `implementation`, `correction`, `review`, `pr-review`, `finalization`) already map one-to-one onto the skills' records. `garage record` needs no change.
- [#37 decision](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/37#issuecomment-6837792244) item 2: string values under a `metadata:` map.
- Each skill already has an "Executing agent identity" section and durable-state marker conventions. The role-rejection and stop rules extend those sections rather than adding parallel ones.

## Expected Change Surface

**Skills:** all five `skills/*/SKILL.md`. Each skill gets:

- the configuration-read step;
- the floor rules it does not yet state in its own text;
- the evidence templates, where it writes records;
- the role metadata;
- the `garage record` step.

**Docs:** replace the statements that the skills do not read configuration yet, in:

- [docs/configuration.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/configuration.md) (the intro and "Absent and invalid configuration");
- the [extension-points.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/extension-points.md) "Configuration format" bullet;
- the [responsibility-floor.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/responsibility-floor.md#current-state) "Current state" section;
- the [review-evidence.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/review-evidence.md) status, because the block stops being informational only;
- the "Until they do" paragraph in [docs/skill-adoption.md](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/blob/fa30a65/docs/skill-adoption.md#configuration).

**Code:** none expected.

## Contracts and Data Impact

- The skills become consumers of configuration schema v2 and of `garage-artifact-v1` and `garage-evidence`.
- `metadata.garage-role` and its values become a contract that #38 consumes.
- No persisted data changes.

## Authorization / Security / Privacy

- An in-session instruction cannot override a configured value or a floor rule. The skill text must say so.
- E8 authorities remain human governance assertions. An agent never fills or substitutes for one.
- `garage record` stays private and non-authoritative. It never gates, authorizes, or advances workflow.

## External Integrations / Operational Concerns

- None beyond GitHub records, which the skills already use.

## Known Environment / Deployment Requirements

- After merge, refresh the installed skill copies in each configured target (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI user paths).
- Answer 1 makes the `garage` binary a runtime requirement for resolving configured values. Nothing installs it yet, because #38 installs skills, not the binary. Agents without it stop at the first extension point they reach.

## Validation Plan

- `make check`, CI's `garage config validate`, and the Markdown link and anchor check.
- Check that the configuration-read step is worded consistently across the five skills.
- Walk through these cases against the skill text:
  - absent configuration;
  - invalid configuration;
  - missing binary;
  - an optional value omitted, so the default applies;
  - a required value (E5, E8) reached;
  - E1 used as the PR target.
- Check every evidence template against review-evidence.md, including `responds_to`, `supplements`, and the resolved `integration_ref`.

## Regression / Adjacent-System Risks

- **The binary dependency** (answer 1) applies to every configured adopter. It must be stated plainly in the skills and docs, so that a stop caused by a missing binary is not mistaken for a configuration defect.
- **Stray untracked files.** `garage-artifact-v1` stages untracked, non-ignored files. Stray files, such as agent worktrees under `.claude/`, therefore change the working-tree changeset. The #35 Agent #1 record worked around this with a clean clone. The skill text should state that the working tree must hold exactly the artifact.
- **The PR-review templates** must keep both minimum triggers (F10) and the issue review's authority exactly as they are.

## Scope Boundaries

**In scope:** everything above.

**Out of scope / follow-up:**

- the meaning of E10 `guidance.conditional` names (answer 4);
- installing skills or the binary, and `metadata.garage-revision` (#38);
- the status view and verifier (#40);
- ignoring `.claude/` or other stray paths in Builder Garage's checkout;
- the open suggestions in #24.

## Unresolved Questions

- **Blocking:** the maintainer records answers 1–4 above on this issue, and the implementation cites that comment.

## Implementation Guidance

- Embed the same configuration-read step in each skill's own text. Installed copies are standalone, and they cannot rely on links to this repository's docs.
- Resolve each extension point where the skill uses it, not up front (answer 2).
- Copy the evidence templates from review-evidence.md. Do not reword their fields.
- Start from `origin/main` on a new branch.

**Readiness-report correction — configuration use and floor rules**

The report’s statement that E5 always requires valid configuration is narrowed. A directly requested discovery invocation may investigate an unconfigured repository. E5 configuration is required only when an agent is deciding whether discovery is warranted under the project’s configured discovery policy.

The report’s statement that each skill receives floor rules it does not yet state is also narrowed. Each skill receives only the responsibility-floor rules it must itself enforce; #33 does not duplicate the complete F1–F14 floor in every skill.

These clarifications preserve the report’s **NOT READY** verdict pending the maintainer decisions below.

## Maintainer decision following the #33 readiness report (2026-11-13)

These decisions follow the [#33 readiness report](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/33#issuecomment-6851439212) and its correction above. This comment does not change repository files or project fields, and it does not create or close issues.

### Decisions

1. **Configuration validity.** A skill treats configuration as valid only when `garage config validate` succeeds. It then reads the needed value from `.garage/config.yaml`. If the binary is unavailable or validation fails, the skill stops and escalates; it never judges validity itself.

2. **Where configuration is read.** A skill resolves configuration only when it reaches an extension point that needs a project value.
   - An absent or invalid required value stops the skill there.
   - A valid omitted optional value uses its declared canonical default.
   - E5 is required only when deciding whether discovery is warranted under project policy; direct requested discovery may proceed without configuration.
   - E8 is required whenever a human authority must be resolved.

3. **Functional skill-role metadata.** `metadata.garage-role` uses:
   - `implementer` for application-implementation-workflow and integration-pr-review;
   - `reviewer` for independent-implementation-review;
   - `readiness` for implementation-readiness-workflow;
   - `discovery` for engineering-discovery-workflow.

   This metadata identifies a skill’s function; it does not replace Agent #1 / Agent #2 boundaries or grant responsibility.

4. **E10 conditional guidance.** The meaning of `guidance.conditional` names is out of scope for #33. Existing conditional guidance, including Supabase guidance, continues to apply under its own stated condition. #33 does not consume those names or turn them into an enablement gate.

### Already decided

- #33 adopts #34’s `garage-evidence` and `garage-artifact-v1` record format, as already decided in the [#33/#35 decision](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/35#issuecomment-6839187808), item 2.
- Each role makes one best-effort `garage record` attempt only after its durable GitHub record has been written and verified. Recording never gates, authorizes, advances, or coordinates workflow.

### Readiness

These decisions clear #33’s readiness blocker.

# Implementation Readiness: #33 — READY

Re-assessed against `main` at `fa30a65`, the same base as the [readiness report](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/33#issuecomment-6851439212). This was read-only.

## Decision

**READY.** The report's only blocker is cleared: the maintainer recorded the four decisions in the [maintainer decision](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/33#issuecomment-6851542937). No new material unknowns were found.

The report applies as narrowed by its [correction](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/33#issuecomment-6851542508):

- **E5.** A directly requested discovery may run without configuration. E5 is required only when an agent is deciding whether discovery is warranted under the project's policy.
- **E8.** It is required whenever a human authority must be resolved.
- **Floor rules.** Each skill states only the rules it must itself enforce, not the complete F1–F14 floor.

## Carried into implementation

- **The `garage` binary.** Decision 1 makes it a runtime requirement for resolving configured values.
- **The working tree.** It must hold exactly the artifact when its `garage-artifact-v1` identity is computed. Stray untracked paths change the changeset.
- **Citations.** The implementation record cites the maintainer decision and the correction above.

[AGENT #1 — IMPLEMENTATION]

```yaml
garage_evidence: 1
record: implementation
issue: 33
checkable:
  artifact:
    method: garage-artifact-v1
    object_format: sha1
    stage: working-tree
    integration_ref: fa30a65b6a4f0ba04414491dda5a94d748469cc2
    base: fa30a65b6a4f0ba04414491dda5a94d748469cc2
    tree: 19a68c2f4a831821eb100cafb7e08cf5635b63d2
    changeset: sha256:689c90510b50a8cde823661c2072271547cc97160bef22ff44d6ff91a4e7914e
    paths: 13
asserted:
  status: ready-for-review
  validation_run: true
```

Status: READY FOR AGENT #2 REVIEW

Artifact/Branch: uncommitted working tree on `feat/33-configuration-aware-skills`, in the git worktree `.claude/worktrees/feat-33` of the main checkout. Base `main` at `fa30a65`. 13 modified paths, +688/−110, no untracked files.

- The identity above was computed in that worktree with the procedure exactly as it is embedded in the skills. The worktree holds exactly the artifact; `garage` and `dist/` are ignored.
- The main checkout's own uncommitted `init` changes, left over from #35 on `feat/35-project-configuration`, are not part of this artifact.

Implemented, following the [readiness report](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/33#issuecomment-6851439212), its [correction](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/33#issuecomment-6851542508), the [#33 maintainer decision](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/33#issuecomment-6851542937) (D1–D4), and the [#33/#35 decision](https://github.com/bdonaldharris/builder-garage/issues/35#issuecomment-6839187808):

- **Configuration read step** (D1, D2; AC1, AC2). The same `# Project configuration` section appears, byte for byte, in the four skills that read configuration. It has three parts:
  - **Resolving.** A value is resolved only when a step that cites an extension point is reached. The skill runs `garage config validate`, then reads `project.<key>`, and an omitted optional key gets the stated default. The skill stops and escalates on a missing binary, failed validation (including an absent file), or a point with no default.
  - **Precedence.** Floor, then valid configuration, then defaults. No other source supplies a project value.
  - **Conflicting instructions.** Instructions that conflict with the role, the valid configuration, or a stated floor rule are rejected.

  Each skill then has an "Extension points this skill uses" table, with the canonical defaults:

  | Skill | Points |
  | --- | --- |
  | implement-workflow | E1, E7, E10 manuals |
  | pr-review | E1, E2, E3, E6, E7, E8 |
  | indep-review | E1, E7 |
  | readiness | E5, E8 |

  Discovery reads no configuration. A directly requested discovery proceeds without it (correction).
- **`staging`** (AC4). It is now only the E1 default. The PR target, the issue branch start, the purpose statement, and `integration_ref` all use E1. The remaining uses of "staging" in the skills name environments.
- **Floor rules.** Each skill states only the rules it must enforce (correction):
  - implement: F1, F3, F4, F5, F8, F9;
  - pr-review: F3, F4, F5, F7, F8, F9, F10, F11, F12;
  - indep-review: F1–F9 and F13, except F2 is stated as an assertion;
  - readiness: F3, F8, F12;
  - discovery: F3, F8.
- **No orchestration** (AC3). The configuration section says configuration never assigns, invokes, schedules, or waits for an agent. The existing terminal-handoff rules are unchanged.
- **Evidence** (#33/#35 decision item 2). The templates adopt `garage-evidence` and `garage-artifact-v1`, with the reference procedure embedded verbatim (checked equal to `docs/review-evidence.md`):
  - the Agent #1 `implementation` and `correction` blocks;
  - the Agent #2 `review` and `pr-review` blocks, with `responds_to`, `supplements`, the recomputed artifact, and `matches_responds_to`;
  - the PR `equivalence` record, with `equivalent_to`.

  `integration_ref` is the resolved object name, never a bare branch. The PR Review Request now carries "Responds to: <equivalence record>". Equivalence is `changeset` equality.
- **Agent #2 prerequisite stop rule.** Agent #2 reviews only when all of these hold; otherwise it stops without a verdict:
  - a well-formed Agent #1 block exists, with the expected record type and a handing-off status;
  - its `integration_ref` is on the E1 branch;
  - the recomputed `changeset` equals the recorded one;
  - for a PR review, an approving issue `review` exists.
- **Record verification and `garage record`** (#33/#35 decision item 4).
  - Agent #1 now reads back and verifies its own records.
  - Each role makes one best-effort `garage record` attempt, only after its GitHub record is verified, using the existing event types and outcomes. A missing binary or a failure is ignored.
- **`metadata.garage-role`** (D3): `implementer` (implement-workflow and pr-review), `reviewer`, `readiness`, `discovery`.
- **Role-based language.** No vendor or tool names remain in the skills: "ChatGPT conversation" became "agent conversation", and "Codex" became "an automated reviewer, whichever tool fills that role (E3)". The Supabase guidance is unchanged and applies under its own condition (D4).
- **Docs.** Each "the skills do not read this yet" statement now describes current behavior, in:
  - `docs/configuration.md`, which gets a new "How the skills read the configuration" section;
  - `docs/extension-points.md`, the "Configuration format" bullet and the E1 default wording;
  - `docs/responsibility-floor.md`, "Current state";
  - `docs/review-evidence.md`:
    - its status is now Adopted;
    - the templates' `integration_ref` uses the resolved object name;
    - an `equivalent_to: none` case is added;
    - the stale "Not decided" item is removed;
  - `docs/skill-adoption.md`;
  - the README limitation;
